newsitem.title: USA: NRC boosts Unicom's Dresden plant rating.
newsitem.headline: NRC boosts Unicom's Dresden plant rating.

text.p: The Nuclear Regulatory Commission (NRC), which last month placed two of Commonwealth Edison Co's nuclear power plants on its watch list, said its latest assessment of the utility's Dresden nuclear power plant awarded a slightly higher rating than in the previous review.
Commonwealth Edison is a unit of Unicom Corp.

The NRC said the Dresden plant received a rating of "good" for operations and plant support and "acceptable" for maintenance and engineering in a Systematic Assessment of Licensee Performance, or SALP, report, which covers the period between March 19, 1995 and December 28, 1996.
The previous rating was "acceptable" for operations, "good" for plant support, "good" for maintenance and "acceptable" for engineering, the NRC said.
The regulatory panel plans to hold a public hearing on the results of the latest SALP report on February 21 at the Dresden facility, which has been on its watch list since 1992.

"We will discuss the report with the utility at the public hearing," NRC spokesman Jan Strasma told Reuters. "The company will have a chance to respond at the meeting, or in writing at a later time, if it wants to challenge any part of the report or add to it."

Meanwhile, the NRC also plans to meet with Commonwealth Edison on February 14 for what it called a "predecisional enforcement conference" to discuss apparent violations at the utility's Quad Cities power plant, and on February 28 to discuss other apparent violations at the Dresden facility.

Separately, Commonwealth Edison said Tuesday it would hold public hearings February 20 on the results of an independent self assessment team that visited its Zion and LaSalle nuclear power plants, which landed on the NRC watch list January 29.
The NRC spokesman said the company will present plans for how it intends to address situations that increased regulatory scrutiny of operations and maintenance at the facilities.
The spokesman characterized Commonwealth Edison's self assessment as a "positive" move for the utility.
Unicom shares closed up 1/8 Tuesday at 22-3/4.
